Maria (runtime): Quick sync — did a short profiling pass on the new microbatch scheduler + chunked prefetch idea. TL;DR: we can hit p95 SLOs with throughput loss or keep throughput and suffer p99 tails. Need prioritization guidance.

Akshay: Can you paste the numbers?

Maria (runtime): Sure. Ran 2k requests with mix: mean prompt 120 tokens, gen 32 tokens. Observed: p50 88ms, p95 210ms, p99 720ms. Prefill vs decode split (p95): prefill ~160ms, decode ~50ms. Full dump: 

```
summary: requests=2000
avg_latency_ms=145
p50_ms=88
p95_ms=210
p99_ms=720
prefill_p95_ms=160
decode_p95_ms=50
kernel_switch_penalty_ms~=8 (when switching quantized->fp kernels)
kv_miss_rate=12%
```

Joel: Ugh kv_miss explains tails — each kv miss does a cold read that blocks the decode path?

Maria (runtime): Right. When microbatching combines requests, KV lookups interleave and we sometimes evict hot KV pages. That causes misses on subsequent decodes, leading to >200ms tail spikes.

Sophia: Did you try sticky scheduling (keep streams on same worker to keep KV warm)?

Maria (runtime): Yes. Sticky reduces kv_miss_rate -> 4% and p99 drops to ~380ms, but overall throughput drops ~7% because some GPUs get hot spots and we lose packing efficiency.

Tyler: What about lowering microbatch size for latency-sensitive routes? e.g., max_batch=4 for routes with SLOs and 16 for background.

Akshay: That was our original thought. But we saw that switching batch sizing per-route increases kernel switch frequency because smaller batches tend to trigger fallbacks to single-stream kernels for short sequences — add 6-10ms per request in some runs.

Maria (runtime): Exactly. Kernel selection is a big part of the overhead. Right now we switch kernels when sequence_length or batch_size crosses heuristics. The switch does buffer reshuffle + memory rebind. We measured median kernel_switch_penalty ~8ms and p99 ~25ms in worst-case.

Joel: Any chance to make kernel selection lazy or iso-task so we don't rebind for every microbatch config change?

Maria (runtime): Possible. Ideas: 1) pre-allocate superset buffers to avoid rebind, 2) unified quantized kernel that handles small batches (best long-term), 3) compile-time kernel variants selected by tiny bitmasks. Tradeoffs: memory vs CPU and dev time.

Sophia: Let's prioritize actions by impact on p99 and implementation cost. My suggestion: A) Sticky scheduling + smarter packing heuristics (low cost, immediate effect) B) Reduce kernel switch penalty (medium cost, high impact) C) Proactive KV prefetch for sticky sessions (medium cost, medium impact) D) Small-batch optimized kernels or quant unified kernels (high cost, high impact).

Maria (runtime): Agree with that ranking. From profiling I add some numbers for prioritization: sticky scheduling reduces p99 by ~48% on current workload; kernel switch fixes estimate p99 reduction ~20-30% and reduces p95 by ~10%; KV prefetch reduces p99 ~30% but costs extra memory/bandwidth; new kernels could shave both p95/p99 by up to 40% but are ~3-6 sprint effort.

Tyler: For immediate follow-ups I can prototype a sticky+pack change and toggleable per-route max_batch in the scheduler. I'll bench with sticky=true/false and with a new packing heuristic (prefer balanced per-GPU fill instead of greedy).

Akshay: Please also add metrics to the trace for kernel_switch (bool), kv_hit (bool), batch_size_at_dispatch (int), and a per-request prefill_time/decode_time tags. We'll need to correlate with p95/p99.

Maria (runtime): Added to the tracking list. Also opened a short runbook entry for oncall: when p99 jumps >2x baseline check kv_miss_rate, kernel_switch_rate, and recent deploys. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/runs/infra-profiles/5678 (internal).

Joel: Nice. Two quick asks: 1) can the scheduler emit a lightweight hint so that backend can prebind likely kernel variant before microbatch arrives? That could reduce switch penalty a lot. 2) add a smoke test that simulates kv thrash patterns so we don't regress.

Maria (runtime): Good points. Action items I captured: 
- Tyler: prototype sticky+balanced packing (ETA 3 days)
- Akshay: add tracing fields and dashboard slices (ETA 2 days)
- Joel: design kernel prebind hint API (we'll iterate) (ETA 1 week)
- Sophia + Maria: scope KV prefetch experiment and memory budget (ETA 1 week)
- All: prepare regression smoke tests for kv thrash + kernel switch (ETA next sprint)

Sophia: Sounds good. My vote is to push sticky+packing first and gate per-route batch size behind the new traces so we can measure impact. :thumbsup:

Tyler: Starting work now, will post benchmark thread here when I have numbers.

Maria (runtime): Thanks everyone. If we can get sticky+packing in and the traces, we should see p99 come down a lot and buy us time for kernel work.

Joel: :thumbsup: keep the notes in the perf doc (linked in the runbook).

Maria (runtime): Will do. Closing thread for now, will reopen with bench numbers.
